issues.evidence: The real Changes panel shows accepted edits, including 'Slide 4 title €71–73m → €74.6m'; the closing promise is 'This time, you checked.' I can see what was proposed, but cannot establish whether another occurrence was missed.
issues.suggested_action: Hold the captured three-file change summary long enough to inspect its scope, and describe the result as reviewing all 10 proposed changes rather than implying the entire pack has been verified.

issues.evidence: The prompt takes DACH Q4 'down to 8.5', the cell changes '8.9 → 8.5', and the memo changes '€71–73m → €74.6m'. As a finance user, I need to understand why lowering an assumption accompanies a higher reported outlook.
issues.suggested_action: Use the existing real Excel view to show the resulting FY26 total of 74.6 alongside the changed DACH cell, then show that total replacing the stale memo and deck range.

issues.evidence: Frames 10 and 13 repeat the head-in-hands reaction; notifications pile up, and the supplied audio timeline adds escalating heartbeats and an echoed third Done chime. The VO says, 'You don't even know what's wrong anymore.'
issues.suggested_action: Remove one repeated reaction and reduce the echoed chime and heartbeat escalation; retain the stopped Send cursor as the main emotional payoff.

issues.evidence: The VO identifies 'the formatting's wrecked' as an early failure, but frame 6 shows a fairly orderly memorandum. The later real demo concentrates on numerical and textual diffs.
issues.suggested_action: Make the opening failure a clearly visible stale table value or one concrete formatting defect, and prioritize the cross-file inconsistency that the real product footage actually resolves.

issues.evidence: The final card says 'Request early access' without telling me what I can evaluate before committing my team's reporting workflow.
issues.suggested_action: Add a short invitation to evaluate a model, memo and deck together using sample files, if that is an available early-access experience.

constraint_failures.rule: Every message holds for at least 2.5 seconds.
constraint_failures.evidence: The supplied timeline gives 'Revenue is now €74.6m, not €71–73m. Fix slide 2.' a 2.4-second hold.

top_revision: Make the real demo visibly connect the DACH edit to the resulting €74.6m total and the scoped review of 10 proposed changes across three files.
purchase_objections: Can it find the relevant occurrences in my actual pack, including charts and tables, rather than only show the edits it happened to propose?
Will my firm's templates, formulas and native Office files survive the round trip?
Does using another workspace fit our existing Office and linked-reporting workflow?
Our team would need an approved data-handling arrangement before uploading client or portfolio files; this film provides no evidence about that.
I would need to test a representative pack before choosing this over our existing tools.
would_try: yes — the real per-cell controls and cross-file Changes panel address my fear of invisible edits well enough to justify testing sample files.
buy_decision: TRY_FIRST — a successful trial on one representative pack, with independently checked numbers and preserved formatting, would flip me to BUY.
